theory.intro: The **percentage error** compares a measurement's absolute error with the size of the measurement itself. The same absolute error matters far more on a small measurement than on a large one.
facts: The absolute error is half the precision of the measurement.
Unless otherwise stated, precision is the smallest place value of the stated measurement.
The absolute error and the measurement must be in the same units before dividing.
When the measurement size is held constant, a smaller absolute error gives a smaller percentage error. The booklet compares measurements of approximately the same size.

workedExamples.question_text: A parcel is weighed as $24$ kg. Find the percentage error, correct to two decimal places.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The precision is $1$ kg.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Absolute error}&=\tfrac12\times1\\&=0.5\text{ kg}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Percentage error}&=\frac{0.5}{24}\times100\%\\&\approx2.08\%\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text:
Find the percentage error of each measurement, correct to three decimal places.
(a) $4.25$ kg
(b) $36.0$ s, correct to one decimal place
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) The precision is $0.01$ kg.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Absolute error}&=\tfrac12\times0.01\\&=0.005\text{ kg}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Percentage error}&=\frac{0.005}{4.25}\times100\%\\&\approx0.118\%\end{aligned}$
(b) The trailing zero records tenths of a second, so the precision is $0.1$ s.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Absolute error}&=\tfrac12\times0.1\\&=0.05\text{ s}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Percentage error}&=\frac{0.05}{36.0}\times100\%\\&\approx0.139\%\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text:
Find the percentage error of each measurement, correct to two decimal places.
(a) A road measured as $650$ m, to the nearest $10$ m
(b) A ribbon measured as $17.0$ cm, to the nearest $0.5$ cm
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) The stated precision is $10$ m.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Absolute error}&=\tfrac12\times10\\&=5\text{ m}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Percentage error}&=\frac{5}{650}\times100\%\\&\approx0.77\%\end{aligned}$
(b) The stated precision is $0.5$ cm.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Absolute error}&=\tfrac12\times0.5\\&=0.25\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Percentage error}&=\frac{0.25}{17.0}\times100\%\\&\approx1.47\%\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A container's capacity is measured as $1.85$ L, correct to the nearest $10$ mL. Find the percentage error, correct to two decimal places.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The precision is $10$ mL.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Absolute error}&=\tfrac12\times10\\&=5\text{ mL}\end{aligned}$
Convert the measurement to millilitres before dividing.
$\begin{aligned}1.85\text{ L}&=1.85\times1000\text{ mL}\\&=1850\text{ mL}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Percentage error}&=\frac{5}{1850}\times100\%\\&\approx0.27\%\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: An object is weighed as $20$ kg and then as $20.3$ kg using a more precise scale. Calculate each percentage error, correct to two decimal places, and explain why the second is smaller.
workedExamples.solution_text:
For $20$ kg, the precision is $1$ kg.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Absolute error}&=\tfrac12\times1\\&=0.5\text{ kg}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Percentage error}&=\frac{0.5}{20}\times100\%\\&=2.50\%\end{aligned}$
For $20.3$ kg, the precision is $0.1$ kg.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Absolute error}&=\tfrac12\times0.1\\&=0.05\text{ kg}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Percentage error}&=\frac{0.05}{20.3}\times100\%\\&\approx0.25\%\end{aligned}$
The measurements are nearly the same size. The second absolute error is ten times smaller, giving a much smaller percentage error.

foundation.question_text:
A suitcase is weighed as $32$ kg.
Find the percentage error of this measurement, correct to two decimal places.
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Identify the precision.**
$\text{Precision} = 1$ kg
2. **Find the absolute error.**
$\tfrac{1}{2} \times 1 = 0.5$ kg
3. **Apply the percentage error formula.**
$\dfrac{0.5}{32} \times 100\%$
$= 1.5625\%$
$\approx 1.56\%$

development.question_text:
A box of books is weighed once as $14$ kg and again, on a more precise scale, as $14.2$ kg.
Find the percentage error of each measurement, correct to two decimal places, and explain why the second is smaller.
development.solution_text:
$14$ kg: absolute error $= 0.5$ kg
$\dfrac{0.5}{14} \times 100\% \approx 3.57\%$
$14.2$ kg: absolute error $= 0.05$ kg
$\dfrac{0.05}{14.2} \times 100\% \approx 0.35\%$
The measurements are almost the same size, but the second absolute error is ten times smaller, so its percentage error is much smaller.

mastery.question_text:
A fence is measured as $7$ m to the nearest metre, and again as $680$ cm to the nearest $10$ cm.
Find both percentage errors correct to two decimal places, and state which measurement has the smaller percentage error.
mastery.solution_text:
$7$ m: absolute error $= 0.5$ m
$\dfrac{0.5}{7} \times 100\% \approx 7.14\%$
$680$ cm: absolute error $= 5$ cm
$\dfrac{5}{680} \times 100\% \approx 0.74\%$
$0.74\% < 7.14\%$, so the $680$ cm measurement has the smaller percentage error.
